questions.q: What were the main features of the Bhakti movement?
answer: The Bhakti movement was a great wave of devotional religion that spread across India from about the eighth century, and it had several important features.

answer.text: Its central idea was intense personal devotion, or bhakti, to a chosen god, such as Vishnu, Shiva or the Goddess. Salvation was to be won not through elaborate ritual or priestly mediation but through love and surrender to god.
The saints preached the equality of all before god and rejected caste distinctions and empty ritual. Saints came from all sections, including women like Mirabai and Andal, and low-caste devotees.
Some, following saguna bhakti, worshipped god with form, as Tulsidas and Surdas did; others, following nirguna bhakti, worshipped a formless god, as Kabir and Guru Nanak did.
The saints composed in the languages of the common people, so their message spread widely.

answer: Thus the Bhakti movement made religion simple, personal and inclusive.
